label: NEGATIVE/FOUND
role: Small-M BF16 GEMM for the attention prefix (6144->2624/2752, 78 calls/step) and q_b (2048->8192/12288, 78 calls/step).
pcvs: M (hd_out) 64..256, K (hd_in) 512..2048, tile_m 16/32, tokens 1..4 (small instantiations; production extrapolated)
finding: Exact: global_unique_read_bytes = 2*M*K + 2*tokens*K, tensor_float_flops = 16*M*K for any tokens, blocks = M/tile_m. Hypothesis from CTA counts: the prefix shapes launch 82/86 CTAs on 148 SMs (one CTA/SM), so they should be 1.72x slower than balanced. A standalone B300 benchmark (HBM-resident weights) refuted it: tile_m 16 (164/172 CTAs) is 0.68-0.97x of the current speed; current 7.3-7.9 us = 4.1-4.4 TB/s. The same sweep found that the hd_in 2048 shapes run faster with 4 pipeline stages instead of 8 (98 KB -> 49 KB shared, 2 -> 4 CTAs/SM, 512/768 CTAs from ~1.7/2.6 waves to one): 2048->8192 9.00 -> 7.65 us, 2048->12288 12.5 -> 11.4 us, bitwise. The new latency_report residency columns (CTAs/SM from shared memory and threads, waves) expose that wave structure directly.
timing: Standalone B300 (b108): see finding. In-graph b101 CUPTI (inclusive, PDL): 2624 7.8, 2752 11.8, 8192 14.2, 12288 17.9 us.
credit: DrPerf supplied the exact work interface and the (wrong) coverage hypothesis; the GPU sweep found the stage effect; the residency view in latency_report was added afterwards so DrPerf flags wave structure.
